title: Coupled Resonator Filter - n78 (3.3-3.8 GHz 5G NR) for Public Safety Band Filter
subtitle: Design Validation and Performance Characterization
author: Dr. Lena Kowalski

sections.1_OBJECTIVE: This document describes the design, simulation, and characterization of a Coupled Resonator Filter filter targeting n78 (3.3-3.8 GHz 5G NR) for Public Safety Band Filter. The filter is designed on Langasite substrate with a target center frequency of 1971.3 MHz and bandwidth of 175.0 MHz. The objective is to validate that the filter meets the required insertion loss, rejection, and linearity specifications for integration into the Public Safety Band Filter module. This design iteration addresses feedback from the previous revision regarding out-of-band rejection improvements and temperature stability.
sections.2_SCOPE:
- Filter Type: Coupled Resonator Filter
- Frequency Band: n78 (3.3-3.8 GHz 5G NR)
- Application: Public Safety Band Filter
- Substrate: Langasite
- Package: SiP (System in Package)
- Design Tool: Cadence AWR Microwave Office
- Design Center: Cedar Rapids Lab

This specification applies to all variants of the Coupled Resonator Filter design targeting n78 (3.3-3.8 GHz 5G NR). Results are used to qualify the design for mass production release.
sections.3_DESIGN_PARAMETERS:
Center Frequency:       1971.3 MHz
Bandwidth (3 dB):       175.0 MHz
Insertion Loss Target:  <= 3.5 dB
Return Loss Target:     >= 23.0 dB
Out-of-Band Rejection:  >= 42.0 dB
Isolation (Duplexer):   >= 21.0 dB
Q Factor:               1960
Temperature Coefficient:-15.2 ppm/°C
Die Size:               0.9 x 2.2 mm
Wafer Size:             6-inch
Number of Resonators:   10
Electrode Material:     Mo
Passivation:            SiO2
sections.4_TEST_PROCEDURE:
1. Open Cadence AWR Microwave Office and load the Coupled Resonator Filter template project.
2. Define the substrate stack: Langasite with specified layer thicknesses.
3. Set design targets: center freq 1971.3 MHz, BW 175.0 MHz.
4. Run initial EM simulation with 2D mesh density of 20 cells/wavelength.
5. Optimize resonator geometry using gradient descent (target IL < 3.5 dB).
6. Verify coupling coefficients between resonator stages.
7. Run 3D FEM simulation to account for package parasitics (SiP (System in Package)).
8. Export GDS-II layout for mask fabrication.
9. Fabricate prototype wafers (6-inch, Langasite).
10. Perform on-wafer probing using Anritsu MS46122B ShockLine.
11. Measure S-parameters (S11, S21, S12, S22) from 100 MHz to 5914 MHz.
12. Compare measured results against simulation and specification limits.
13. Perform temperature cycling (-40°C to +85°C) and re-measure.
14. Document results and generate summary report.
sections.5_ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- Insertion loss at center frequency shall be <= 3.5 dB
- Return loss in passband shall be >= 23.0 dB
- Out-of-band rejection at +/- 262 MHz offset >= 42.0 dB
- Group delay variation across passband shall be <= 7 ns
- Temperature drift over -40°C to +85°C shall be <= 3.7 MHz
- Power handling shall be >= +34 dBm at 1 dB compression
- ESD tolerance >= 2000 V (HBM)
- Die yield on qualification lot >= 87%
sections.6_TEST_RESULTS:
Measurement Date:       2024-08-23
Devices Tested:         93
Insertion Loss (meas):  3.25 dB
Return Loss (meas):     24.8 dB
Rejection (meas):       44.6 dB
Isolation (meas):       26.4 dB
Q Factor (meas):        1960
Group Delay Variation:  6.4 ns
Power Handling:         +32 dBm
Die Yield:              91.0%

Result Classification:  NEEDS REVIEW
sections.7_OBSERVATIONS:
a) The Coupled Resonator Filter design demonstrated below-target performance for n78 (3.3-3.8 GHz 5G NR).
b) Insertion loss is marginally above target; electrode thickness optimization recommended.
c) Out-of-band rejection exceeded the minimum requirement.
d) Package parasitic effects were consistent with 3D EM model predictions.
e) Cross-talk between adjacent filter channels was below -55 dB.
sections.8_CORRECTIVE_ACTIONS:
1. Review near-band rejection margin for worst-case temperature.
2. Re-run EM simulation with refined mesh for better accuracy.
3. Schedule follow-up measurement after design tweak.
